title: ci: Test Core's two timing gates exit-grade on `schedule` alone (C2), with a 20s ceiling floor
body:
Fixes #22949
Clause-②: no (internal CI tooling; no published surface)
Refs #22966
Refs #22968

Implements ruling [6119186511](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/22949#issuecomment-6119186511) (letter C2 for both timing steps, plus an absolute floor; the maintainer's word 「当然短期先尽快修复」): **a timing gate exit-grades only on the run profile its baseline was measured on; everywhere else it reports.** #22966 (the PR-time drift card) is the drift half of the same ruling and remains open for triage. #22968 (the hourly card) remains open until an uneventful green hourly run after this lands.

## What changes

| Step (`ci.yml`) | `schedule` | `merge_group`, `pull_request`, `push`, `workflow_dispatch` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `Test Core` → "Check the per-package suite-duration ceilings" | unchanged: a package over its ceiling exits 1 with an `::error::` annotation | the same table prints, each package over its ceiling is a `::warning::` annotation, exit 0 |
| `Test Core (N/6)` → "Check this shard's timing drift" | unchanged: DRIFT past 1.5x exits 1 (and withholds the shard attestation) | the same verdict text prints, the DRIFT is one `::warning::` annotation, exit 0 |

- **Absolute floor (ceiling step only):** a package whose effective ceiling is under 20 s (`CEILING_FLOOR_SECONDS`) is never red on any event and prints `below floor`. A ceiling at the floor is graded; a ruled raise that lifts a ceiling to the floor or above grades the package again.
- **Unchanged:** the formula (window max x 1.25), `RULED_CEILING_RAISES`, the Q2 B rule for new packages, the dataset and the refresh lane. No edit to `scripts/test-shard-timings.json`, `scripts/measure-test-shard-timings.mjs` or `.github/workflows/shard-timings-refresh.yml`.
- **Refusals stay red on every event.** A malformed raise record or ceiling table, or a missing `--event`, is not a timing reading and does not vary with runner load, so it exits 1 everywhere. The raise record is already checked at PR time by lint.yml's `--self-test` ("the live record is well-formed"). This is my reading of the ruling's scope (it names "every package over its ceiling or shard over its drift bound"); if the seat reads it as "the step never exits 1 off schedule", the change is small and local to the two render functions.
- **`workflow_dispatch` reports.** The ruling names `schedule` as the one exit-graded event. The refresh lane reads `event=schedule` runs only (`DEFAULT_RUN_EVENT` in `scripts/ci/select-shard-timings-run.mjs`, no `--event` override in `shard-timings-refresh.yml`), and a dispatched run writes the remote turbo cache (`TURBO_CACHE` `rw`) where the hourly run only reads it, so it is not the baseline's profile.

## H2: how the off-schedule path is spelled

Both scripts take a **required** `--event`, and ci.yml passes `--event "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME"`. The rule (`TIMING_GRADED_EVENT = 'schedule'`, `timingGateMode`, `timingModeNote`) is defined once, in `scripts/partition-test-shards.mjs`, and imported by `scripts/check-test-suite-ceilings.mjs` (which already imported `escapeWorkflowCommandMessage` from there).

- Why not `continue-on-error` (the `ci.yml:1204` spelling): it leaves the `::error::` annotations in place and does not produce the `::warning::` the ruling asks for.
- Why not an opt-in `--report-only` set by a YAML expression: the policy would then live in an expression no self-test reads, and a typo in it fails silently in one direction or the other. With `--event`, the decision table is self-tested in the script, and a missing or empty event is **refused** (exit 1), never defaulted to either mode.
- Neither step gains an `if:` or a `continue-on-error`. The drift step's comment block carries "NO `if:` and NO `continue-on-error` (the red is the point)"; that line still holds as written and is extended, not removed. The other ⛔ lines H1 named (`ci.yml:1036`-`1037` and `:1218`) bind the attestation pair, which this PR does not touch.
- The drift verdict was measured first: in graded mode DRIFT prints to stderr with **no** annotation (pinned by the existing self-test), so `partition-test-shards.mjs --check-drift` needed the same flag for a warning to exist at all.

## The floor: 20 s, and its reading

Read by the `domain:devx` seat off the table's distribution, as the ruling assigns: on `1f312fdfa` (unchanged at this PR's base `246edf5b3`) the 72 ceilings run 3.40, 3.69, 4.24, 5.18, 6.39, 9.10 and 16.23 s, then 22.71 s (`downstream-contract`) and up. 20 s sits in the widest gap of the low band (16.23 to 22.71). Seven packages fall under it: `knowledge-ragflow`, `service-cache`, `observability`, `sdui-parser`, `knowledge-memory`, `embedder-openai`, `client-react`. The value, its reading and the ruling URL are recorded once, in the gate header ("The absolute floor").

## H5: packages the hourly run never grades

The hourly run grades only the packages it executes; a turbo cache replay carries no window. I read the "How much of the run this table saw" block of six hourly `schedule` runs (MCP `get_job_logs` on each `Test Core` job; the 04:09Z set is the complement of that run's graded rows against the 72-package dataset, since the tail read missed its block):

| Run | Time (2026-10-12) | Replayed packages |
|:--|:--|--:|
| `38192273698` | 01:32Z | 12 |
| `38195222269` | 02:17Z | 5 |
| `38198819852` | 03:12Z | 27 |
| `38202645321` | 04:09Z | 14 |
| `38206660804` | 05:08Z | 15 |
| `38210849670` | 06:05Z | 11 |

- **Replayed on every one of the six runs: none.** The 02:17Z run replayed only `formula`, `metadata-fs`, `observability`, `sdui-parser` and `spec`.
- **Replayed on all three runs since the table went live (04:09Z, 05:08Z, 06:05Z): `core`, `metadata`, `plugin-hono-server`.** Each was also replayed at 01:32Z and 03:12Z (5 of 6); the one run that executed them (02:17Z) predates the ceiling table, so none of the three has been graded yet. `formula`, `metadata-fs` and `spec` were replayed on 4-5 of the 6.
- **Handling, as the ruling leaves it:** graded on any hourly run that executes them, report-only everywhere else. No mechanism forces them to execute (not in the ruling); I do not think one is needed yet, because the replay set rotates run to run, and the gate header now states the blind spot.

## Parity checkers

None was touched; none needed an edit. Run green on the head unchanged: `check-self-test-workflow-commands`, `check-step-collectors`, `check-workflow-status-functions`, `check-required-contexts`, `check-aggregator-roster`, `check-ratchet-remedy-authority`, `check-stall-guard-budget`, `check-stall-guard-headroom`, `check-workflow-step-name-quoting`, `check-shard-attestation`. H3 ("expect at least one to need a matching edit") did not hold.

## Evidence (head `ef3d0764b`)

**Ceiling CLI, one synthetic capture** (`cloud-connection` 200.33 s vs 163.89 s, `downstream-contract` 25.00 s vs 22.71 s, `knowledge-ragflow` 4.80 s vs 3.40 s, `client` 150.00 s vs 179.74 s, against the live dataset):

```text
--event schedule      EXIT=1
::error title=Suite-duration ceiling::@objectstack/cloud-connection: 200.33s, over its 163.89s ceiling. ...
::error title=Suite-duration ceiling::@objectstack/downstream-contract: 25.00s, over its 22.71s ceiling. ...
  --    @objectstack/knowledge-ragflow: 4.80s against 3.40s (1.41x) -- below floor: a ceiling under 20s is never red
  exit-graded: a `schedule` run is the profile the baseline was measured on.

--event merge_group   EXIT=0
::warning title=Suite-duration ceiling::@objectstack/cloud-connection: 200.33s, over its 163.89s ceiling. ... Report only on a `merge_group` run: ...
::warning title=Suite-duration ceiling::@objectstack/downstream-contract: 25.00s, over its 22.71s ceiling. ... Report only on a `merge_group` run: ...
  (the same stderr table, line for line, ending)
  report only: a `merge_group` run is not the profile the baseline was measured on (`schedule`), so a red reading is a warning here and the step exits 0.

no --event            EXIT=1   Error: the run's event is null. ... A missing event is refused rather than guessed.
```

**Drift CLI, one synthetic turbo summary** (`runtime` 916.1 s, `service-analytics` 463.7 s, `client` 183.5 s against the live weights = 1.82x):

```text
--event schedule      EXIT=1   stdout empty; stderr "shard-timing-drift: DRIFT -- Test Core (6/6), 1563.3s measured vs 860.2s predicted ... = 1.82x" + "exit-graded: ..."
--event pull_request  EXIT=0   one "::warning title=Test Core shard timing drift::Test Core (6/6): ... past the red bound. ... Report only on a `pull_request` run: ..." + the same stderr text ending "report only: ..."
no --event            EXIT=1   Error: the run's event is null. ...
```

**Self-tests:** `check-test-suite-ceilings --self-test` OK, 58 cases across 9 batteries (two new: the floor, 8 cases; off-`schedule` reporting, 8 cases; roster floor 7 to 9). `partition-test-shards --self-test` OK (one new battery, 8 cases; roster floor 12 to 13).

**Ablations** (each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor hit 1 to 0, restored to the HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty after):
- floor removed (the comparison against `CEILING_FLOOR_SECONDS` in `gradeCeilings` rewritten to compare against 0): ceiling self-test red, `floor: a 3.40s ceiling run at 4.20s read over / OVER, exit 1`.
- `timingGateMode` always `'grade'`: partition self-test red (`C2: merge_group, pull_request, push, workflow_dispatch exit-grade, but only schedule may`) and ceiling self-test red (`floor: a 22.71s ceiling run at 25s off schedule was not a warning alone: exit 1`).

**Gates:** `dispatch-gates --commands` on this diff derives 59 commands (the same 59 as at dispatch); `--ran` reconciliation: 59 accounted, 55 exit 0, 4 NOT MEASURED (exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET: `check:dts-closure`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content` read built `dist/`; this diff touches no package, so no build is owed and CI runs them). `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates`: fast tier 1828 cases, exit 0. The 9 workflow-valued families (the ceiling step's own `--captures` run among them) are CI's.

**Lint, narrowed:** eslint over the two edited scripts, 2 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings (`--format json`). Population: `eslint.config.mjs` lints `**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}`, so both are in it; ci.yml is not eslint's. Invariance: the config enables no type-aware linting (`--print-config` shows `parserOptions` without `project`), so this diff cannot move a verdict on any untouched file.

## Acceptance notes

- Size: 502 added / 84 removed lines over 3 files; about half the additions are the three new self-test batteries, most of the rest is header and step-comment prose. The shape is the one H6 listed (two step edits, one flag in two scripts, a header, self-test cases).
- `ci.yml`'s comment above "Download this run's shard test timings" still says the ceiling check "is the one step here that DOES red the job". It remains true on `schedule`; I left it as is because the file surface is the two timing steps. Carrier: none.
